Black Friday sales have officially gone live at Amazon, Walmart, and Best Buy. Despite the fact that PC prices are trending in the wrong direction recently, there are plenty of solid Black Friday deals to be found to help alleviate the financial sting of your next PC upgrade. I've rounded up the best deals from the major retailers below and I will continue to update this list with more discounted configurations as they go live through Black Friday and Cyber Monday.

The Best Black Friday Gaming PC Deals So Far

Alienware Aurora RTX 5070 Gaming PC for $1,899

If you're looking for a solid deal on an Alienware gaming PC for Black Friday, your best bet seems to be from Amazon rather than Dell itself. For a limited time, you can pick up a brand new Alienware Aurora RTX 5070 gaming PC for $1,899.999 with free shipping. An identical configuration would cost $800 more if you purchased it directly from Dell. Amazon labels this as a Black Friday deal, but there is a good chance this deal will sell out well before November 27.

This Alienware Aurora gaming PC is equipped with an air-cooled Intel Core Ultra 7 265F CPU, GeForce RTX 5070 12GB GPU, 32GB of DDR5-5200MHz RAM, and a 1TB SSD. The GeForce RTX 5070 is the best value Nvidia card for 1080p and 1440p gaming. It's also powerful enough to run most games at 4K, although at that point you'll see noticeable gains jumping up to a 5070 Ti. Check out our RTX 5070 review.

CyberPowerPC RTX 5060 Ti Gaming PC for $1,280

For Black Friday, Amazon is offering the CyberPowerPC RTX 5060 Ti gaming PC for just $1,279.99 with free shipping after a 15% off instant discount. It's equipped with an AMD Ryzen 7 8700F CPU, GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 8GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and 1TB NVMe SSD. The RTX 5060 Ti graphics card is a great GPU for 1080p gaming. It outperforms the RTX 4060 Ti by about 20%, and the gap widens in games that support DLSS 4.5. Note that this model has 8GB of VRAM, which means that although it will play most games at 1440p quite well, it will struggle with more demanding games that use a lot of VRAM. At that point I'd suggest jumping to an RTX 5070.

ABS Cyclone RTX 5060 Gaming PC for $749

Shopping around for a budget PC under $1,000? For Black Friday, the ABS Cyclone gaming PC with GeForce RTX 5060 graphics card drops to just $749 shipped. Despite the low price tag, this PC is still (much) more powerful than the more expensive Steam Machine and will get you a consistent 60fps in most games at 1080p.

This system is equipped with an Intel Core i5-14400F CPU, GeForce RTX 5060 GPU, 16GB of DDR4-3200MHz RAM, and a 1TB NVMe SSD. The RTX 5060 outperforms its predecessor the RTX 4060 by about 20%-30% and that's before factoring in DLSS. This is a solid budget option for 1080p gaming and you should be able to squeeze consistent 60fps+ framerate out of just about any game. If you're gunning for higher resolutions like 1440p or 4K, however, you'll definitely want to upgrade to an RTX 5060 Ti (16GB) or better.

HyperX Omen RTX 5080 Gaming PC for $2,700

The unassuming design of the HyperX Omen 35L belies the fact that this is (so far) the most powerful gaming PC on the list. Currently this is the only RTX 5080 equipped gaming PC I can find for under $3,000. The system is equipped with an Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus CPU, GeForce RTX 5080 16GB GPU, 16GB of DDR5 RAM, and a 1TB SSD.

Performance-wise, the RTX 5080 is no slouch. It's one of the fastest cards on the market, bested only by the $2,000 (retail) RTX 5090 and the discontinued $1,600 (retail) RTX 4090. You'll be able to play latest, most demanding games in 4K resolution at high settings and ray tracing enabled. The DLSS 4.5 update has further optimized multi-frame gen and upscaling so you can push really high framerates even in 4K. Check out our Nvidia GeForce RTX 5080 FE review.
